text:
Montreal arrives on a three-game-old sting: the Canadiens blew a two-goal lead to San Jose and lost 4-3 in overtime on Macklin Celebrini's goal. They're 3-1-1 in their last five, but without Nick Suzuki, Ivan Demidov and Florian Xhekaj. With Suzuki out, Cole Caufield is next in line for his minutes. Chicago, rested after five days off, was shut out 4-0 by Dallas last time and sits 2-3-0 in its last five, without Andrew Mangiapane. Ian Cole plays his 1,000th NHL game for the Blackhawks.

Montreal has controlled more of the play. At five on five, it has taken 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games, against 41% for Chicago, and the model projects 3.24 goals for the Canadiens to 3.01 for the Blackhawks. The catch is discipline: Montreal takes 5.4 penalties a game, and Chicago's power play makes 0.40 expected goals a game. In net, projected starters Jacob Fowler (+1.99 goals saved above expected, meaning goals prevented beyond what the shots should have allowed) and Spencer Knight (-0.65) have opposite starts, though Knight was +11.11 over 55 games last season to Fowler's +5.98 over 17.

Connor Bedard (37% to score, 73% for a point) and Caufield (41%, 66%) lead the watch list. Patrick Kane is 63% for a point. Ice Sheet's under-the-radar pick is Roman Kantserov, 56% for a point against a season-pace 35%, because his line creates chances.
